$comment: Capability sets (plan §6.5, §7.2.4, ADR-0008): who may do what, as data. Default deny; a deny always beats an allow. agent:capped is v1's server/capped.js and the refusals in routes/control.js, internal.js and connectors.js, in v1's words. plugin:<id> sets come from each plugin's manifest permissions, crew:<name> and pane:<id> are made on demand.
cappedRefusal: Refused: this task was started from a channel with a mode cap, so it can't {what}. Say so in your report; the user can do it in wisp.

deny.why: install a plugin: the user installs plugins
reach other machines from a grid box
be one of your computers: a box never gets a laptop token
update wisp on a grid box: the grid does
show a desktop notification on a grid box
run a process outside the box sandbox

aboveMode.why: start a task at {label}, above this task’s {cap}
switch a task to {label}, above this task’s {cap}

capped.what: run anything on another machine or in a sandbox
start a task in another project
read a task of another project
act on a task it didn’t start
read or change the user's connectors
put anything on a public link, or take one down
change an item of another project
save a file from outside its folder
read an item of another project
show a file from outside its folders
read a PR by URL: give its number in this task’s repo
put the user’s crew on a link
read a member of another project
read a task of another project
reveal a .env value the user hid

deny.why: change the crew it belongs to
share the crew it belongs to

pane.$comment: A pane holding tasks:write only proposes (v1 pane-card.js): wisp's page shows its prompt on a card and you send it as yourself. Whatever it was allowed, it never starts or sends a task, nor widens its own grant (F-stuff-8).

deny.why: Refused: a pane can only propose a prompt. wisp's page shows it on a card and you start the task (wisp.tasks.launch).
Refused: a pane can only propose a prompt. wisp's page shows it on a card and you send the follow-up (wisp.tasks.followUp).
Refused: a pane can only propose a prompt. wisp's page shows it on a card and you send it.
Refused: a pane can only propose a prompt. wisp's page shows it on a card and you start the task.
Refused: a pane can only propose a prompt. wisp's page shows it on a card and you start the task.
Refused: a pane can't widen its own grant. You allow what it asks for from its bar.
